content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 853 bytes (min+gzip), 102 bytes of which is my own code. Lodash isn't installed in this project, so I couldn't bundle or run the original. I compared against lodash's `startCase`, `merge` and `isEmpty` from what I know of their behaviour, not by running them.

The project-wide `tsc` run still reports errors, but they all come from `src/module.ts`, which still imports lodash. I didn't see any errors for `out/module.ts` in the tail I looked at. I didn't run a type check on `out/module.ts` alone.

| Function | Before | After | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applyPatch` | lodash `merge` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` | Behaves the same on the input range. It mutates `base` and returns it, merging arrays index by index like lodash. |
| `toTitle` | lodash `startCase` | `words(key).map(upperFirst).join(' ')` | A small adapter over library calls, not a hand-written replacement. |
| `isBlank` | lodash `isEmpty` | `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat` | `es-toolkit` has no `isEmpty`, and strings, arrays, objects, numbers and null all need handling. |

- **`startCase` in `es-toolkit`:** it lowercases the rest of each word. `FOO bar` becomes `Foo Bar` instead of lodash's `FOO Bar`, and `XMLHttp` becomes `Xml Http`. Your input range allows consecutive capitals, so that would change results.
- **`startCase` in `es-toolkit/compat`:** it matches lodash, but the bundle came to 2288 bytes.
- **Adapter:** on the 8 sample strings I tried, including `Width.91-ApiWidth.` and `FOO bar`, it gave the same output as the compat version. The bundle is about a third the size, at 853 bytes. I did not test your two `applyPatch` example inputs or any `isBlank` inputs.

`src/module.ts` is unchanged, and nothing was installed. I also left a leftover `out/m2.ts` from my size comparison, which you can delete.
